method: log-evidence-only (no nsys / no torch.profiler yet — pod-auth-pending)
primary_bottleneck: autoregressive-decode + dac-decode (production rate, not first-byte latency)

evidence.interpretation: Fish's HTTP TTFB is 7ms (network is fine). Full synth takes 4824ms wall to produce 2368ms of audio. Realtime factor (RTF) = 4824/2368 = 2.04 — Fish generates audio at half the playback rate. After the initial frames, the WebRTC audio buffer underruns. User-perceived experience: 'instant first word, then pauses.'

deployment_inconsistency_flagged.issue: infra/b300/services/fish-speech/server.py declares /tts (24kHz) but fish_speech_tts.py posts to /v1/tts (44.1kHz). Health probe to /healthz returns 404 → upstream tools/api_server.py from fishaudio/fish-speech is what's actually running, not the committed wrapper. Container also runs on PyTorch 25.02 base — SGLang installed via pip likely older than 25.11.
deployment_inconsistency_flagged.implication: The CUDA-graph + paged-KV defaults in SGLang have improved significantly since 0.4.0. A PyTorch 25.09+ container with sglang>=0.4.7 may already engage these flags by default and cut RTF substantially with zero kernel work.

routing_recommendation:
kernel-author try in this order:
  1. PyTorch container bump 25.02 → 25.09 + sglang>=0.4.7. Engage default CUDA graph capture. Estimate: 4-8h to rebuild + ship + measure. Risk: container compile time on B300, SGLang ABI changes.
  2. If #1 yields RTF >= 1.0, dispatch speculative-decoding for text2semantic. Use a small draft model (1B distillation of Fish text2semantic). Estimate: 16-24h.
  3. If #1 + #2 yield RTF >= 0.5, NVFP4 calibration of Fish weights via SGLang's NVFP4 path. Estimate: 16-24h, real risk of voice-quality regression.

DO NOT pursue: TensorRT-LLM (no Fish recipe), NVIDIA Dynamo (multi-node only).
confidence: medium — without Nsight or torch.profiler we can't see GPU-side kernel timeline. But log evidence + B300 utilization snapshot (0% idle, 30GB/275GB used) makes the autoregressive-decode hypothesis the highest-likelihood. Strongly recommend a 2h Nsight or torch.profiler run to confirm before committing 4-8h to container rebuild.
next_step: operator authorizes one of: (a) nsys install on pod (~30 min setup, gold-standard diagnosis), or (b) torch.profiler script SCP'd to pod + run via SSH (~15 min, no apt install, slightly weaker timeline). Either confirms whether the CUDA-graph-capture hypothesis is correct.
scribe_handoff: Local-evidence triangulation: Fish RTF 2.04 is the bottleneck; first-byte already 7ms. Highest-leverage 48h fix: container bump to PyTorch 25.09 + sglang 0.4.7+ (engages SGLang's CUDA graph defaults). Stretch: speculative decoding. Need profiler run to confirm before committing.
